title: fix(core): refuse a single-record action's row count before its dialog, and translate the refusal (objectui#13384)
body:
Closes #13384
Clause-②: yes (widening: ActionRunnerHandler / ServerActionHandler gain optional refuseBeforeInput; ServerActionRecordIdResolution gains optional errorKey; nothing is refused)

## What changed

A single-record action launched from a list toolbar with 0 or 2+ rows selected is now refused before any confirmation or param dialog opens. It gets the same toast as before and sends nothing. With exactly one row the dialog behaves as before. The refusal is also translated now: it read English under zh-CN.

- **`@object-ui/core` `ActionRunner`**: `ActionRunnerHandler` gains an optional `refuseBeforeInput(action, context)`. `execute` asks the handler it will dispatch to, after the `condition` / `disabled` gates and before `confirmText` and the param collection. A refusal goes through the usual post-execution (error toast, `onFailure`), and nothing is dispatched. If the refusal names an `errorKey`, the runner translates it through `setTranslator`'s translator, with the English as default. This is the same channel the runner's own `RUNNER_TEXT` uses, so core still takes no i18n dependency.
- **`@object-ui/core` `serverActionHandler`**:
  - The two refusal strings come from a keyed table (`actions.selectExactlyOneRow`, `actions.selectRowFirst`).
  - `resolveServerActionRecordId` returns the key as `errorKey` beside the English `error`.
  - `createServerActionHandler` attaches `refuseBeforeInput`, which runs the same resolver the dispatch runs, including an injected `resolveRecordId`. So a record page, which resolves against its own record, is never refused.
  - It skips the early check when the dialog itself collects a param named `recordId`.
  - The check at dispatch time stays for callers that invoke the handler directly.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` `createConsoleServerActionHandler`**: forwards `refuseBeforeInput` from core's handler, which it builds with the wrapper's own `resolveRecordId`. Without the forward the runner never saw the member and the console kept its dialog-first order.
- **`@object-ui/i18n`**: both keys are added to all ten packs. No German low-high quote span is added, so the `de-quote-pairing-3876` counts are unchanged.
- One changeset: core, i18n and app-shell, patch.

Why the runner asks the handler instead of holding the row rule itself: on a record page, a related-list grid publishes `selectedRecords: []` into the page's runner context. A runner-side copy of the rule would refuse every `record_header` action there. Only the handler knows its own resolver.

## Tests

Run on head `024092b03`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/`, `packages/i18n/`, and the 21 app-shell test files that read `consoleServerAction`, `resolveServerActionRecordId` or `toolbarScriptSelection`: **146/146 files, 2113 passed, 13 skipped**.
- New `ActionRunner.recordRowGuard-13384` (core):
  - 0 rows and 2 rows: the toast shows, no param dialog and no confirmation open, and nothing is sent.
  - 1 row: the dialog opens and the one request carries that row.
  - Controls: an object-level toolbar action with 0 rows still opens its dialog; an injected record resolver is not refused; a dialog that collects `recordId` is not judged early.
  - The translator is asked by key, with the English default; an empty answer falls back to English.
- `serverActionHandler.test.ts`: pins for `errorKey` and `refuseBeforeInput`.
- `consoleServerAction.test.tsx`: pins the forward, both alone and through a real `ActionRunner`. 0 and 2 rows open no dialog, pre-open no tab and send nothing. 1 row opens the dialog.
- `ObjectView.toolbarScriptSelection-12331`: its five 0- and 2-row cases now also assert that no dialog opened, beside the toast and the absent request. Every other claim in that suite is unchanged.
- New `recordSelectionRefusal-13384` (i18n): pins the zh-CN text; every other pack defines both keys with its own text.
- Type-check, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm exec turbo run type-check --concurrency=2`:
  - `--filter=@object-ui/core`: 3/3 tasks
  - `--filter=@object-ui/app-shell`: 30/30 tasks, including `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`: exit 0. Dead-keys is report-only. It lists the two new keys as needs-review, the same class as their `actions.*` siblings, which are also reached only through a key table.
- eslint on the touched files: 0 errors. The warnings are pre-existing `no-explicit-any`; none is added.
- `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new. `check-changeset-presence`: pass.

### Ablation

Each run used `ablation-replace` with on-disk proof, and was restored to `git diff HEAD` empty:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| The runner's early refusal disabled | 5 core cases red (0 rows, 2 rows, confirmation, two translator cases) |
| `errorKey` dropped from the refusal | 4 red |
| The console wrapper's forward deleted | 8 red: 3 in `consoleServerAction.test.tsx`, plus all five 0- and 2-row cases of `ObjectView.toolbarScriptSelection-12331` |

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, still open:** the console `flowHandler` in `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` calls `resolveServerActionRecordId` directly and is not a forwarded handler. A `type: 'flow'` action with params, launched from a list toolbar with 0 or 2+ rows, still opens its dialog first, and its refusal still reads English. It could read the new `errorKey`. That file belongs to objectui#13379's claim, so it was not touched here.
- **Out of scope, still open:** the console wrapper's own `newTabUrl` fast-path refusal ("This action runs on a single record — no record id available.") is still a hard-coded English string with no pack key.

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)
